purpose: This medication is used to treat certain types of breast cancer and stomach cancer that have too much of a protein called HER2 on the cancer cells. It is a biosimilar, meaning it works just like the original trastuzumab (Herceptin) but is made by a different manufacturer. Your doctor may use it alone or along with other cancer treatments.
how_it_works: Think of HER2 as a switch on cancer cells that tells them to grow out of control. Trastuzumab-dttb is like a key that locks onto that switch and turns it off, slowing down or stopping the cancer from growing. It also signals your own immune system to come in and help destroy those cancer cells.
common_side_effects: Some of the most common side effects include feeling tired, nausea, headache, diarrhea, feeling cold or getting chills, fever, and joint or muscle aches. Some people also notice hair thinning, sleep problems, or mild infections. These side effects are usually manageable, so let your care team know if anything bothers you.
warnings: The most serious concern with this medicine is heart problems — it can weaken the heart muscle, so your doctor will check your heart regularly during treatment. It should NOT be used during pregnancy because it can harm the unborn baby; use reliable birth control while on this drug and for several months after. Some people may have serious infusion reactions (like trouble breathing, chills, or low blood pressure) during or after the injection, so you will be monitored closely when receiving it. Tell your doctor right away if you have shortness of breath, swelling in your legs, or an irregular heartbeat.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (a drip into your vein) by a nurse or doctor, usually once every 1 or 3 weeks depending on your treatment plan. The first dose is usually given slowly over about 90 minutes to watch for reactions. If you tolerate it well, later doses may be given over 30 minutes. Your exact dose and schedule will be tailored to your body weight and specific cancer treatment plan.
